subject.title: [Feature]: Make detached longwork final delivery ownership explicit

question: Should this issue remain the canonical place to define detached-longwork final-delivery ownership, and which existing substrate should own the durable owner, target identity, retry, suppression, and delivery-confirmation state?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining choice is a public product/API contract across sessions, channel delivery, plugin hooks, and persisted delivery state, which automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Choose an existing substrate
options.body: Use the current subagent completion/delivery or task-delivery substrate as the owner and request a narrow PR that preserves current defaults while adding an explicit owner-mode contract.

options.title: Move to a narrower canonical issue
options.body: If Slack origin loss, background-work survival, or pending-final recovery is the real owner, move this invariant there and keep this issue only as linked design context.

options.title: Reject explicit owner modes
options.body: Keep completionOwnerKey and current routing heuristics as the supported boundary, accepting that migrated longwork orchestration remains an operator/plugin responsibility.

recommendation.title: Choose an existing substrate
recommendation.body: Use the current subagent completion/delivery or task-delivery substrate as the owner and request a narrow PR that preserves current defaults while adding an explicit owner-mode contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are a recent adjacent contributor and routing-history participant, and this decision needs cross-surface product/API ownership rather than a single file-level code owner.
